topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, themes, and learning outcomes for cancer biology.

topics.label: Biological foundations and experimental modeling of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core biological view of cancer as a stepwise failure of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture, alongside the laboratory models used to study it.

topics.label: Pathological mechanisms and progression of tumor invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors progress from contained, benign lesions to invasive and metastasising malignancies through specific anatomical routes and histological stages.

topics.label: Tumor classification, nomenclature, and clinical causes of morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the diagnostic terminology used to classify neoplasms and explain how both benign and malignant tumors produce clinical harm and fatal complications.

topics.label: Patterns of cancer incidence across human populations and multicellular species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare cancer incidence across human tissue sites, companion animals, and diverse multicellular organisms with developmental programs.

topics.label: Clinical principles and modalities of cancer screening and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the diagnostic challenges of early cancer symptoms and evaluate the methodologies, histology, and efficacy of screening programmes across various organ sites.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical previews
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with a recap of the learning objectives and instructions for upcoming practicals.
